bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar To Develop UAE-Backed Food Processing Park With AIM Global Foundation
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar-UAE Partnership to Boost Food Processing and Investment, MoU Signed at AIM Congress 2026 Bihar's Industries Department signs an MoU with AIM Global Foundation at AIM Congress 2026 to establish an integrated agri-food and food processing cluster. The initiative aims to attract UAE and Gulf region investments, linking Bihar's farmers to global supply chains and boosting industrial growth. India -Oneindia Staff By Oneindia Staff Published: Wednesday, September 9, 2026, 0:01 [IST] Add as a preferred source on Google Bihar is strengthening its efforts to emerge as a preferred destination for investment, innovation and industrial growth. As part of this initiative, the Industries Department, Government of Bihar, exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with AIM Global Foundation at the AIM (Annual Investment Meeting) Congress 2026 in Dubai. The partnership aims to promote the development of a dedicated Food Processing Park in Bihar, supported by investments from the UAE and the wider Gulf region. The MoU exchange took place in the presence of Industries Minister Shreyasi Singh. It was signed by Kundan Kumar, Secretary, Industries Department, Government of Bihar, and H.E. Dawood Al-Shezawi, President, AIM Global Foundation. Mukul Kumar Gupta, Director, Industries, Government of Bihar, was also present on the occasion. The initiative aims to attract UAE and Gulf region investments, linking Bihar's farmers to global supply chains and boosting industrial growth. Switch To Shorts Under the MoU, AIM Global Foundation and the Bihar Industries Department will work towards developing an integrated agri-food and food processing cluster in the state. The initiative will seek to attract investments from companies, institutions and investors based in the UAE and the wider Gulf region. It aims to leverage Bihar's agricultural strengths and position the state as an important sourcing and processing base for food supply chains serving Gulf markets. Partnership to Open Global Opportunities for Bihar's Farmers and Industries Industries Minister Shreyasi Singh said the partnership with AIM Global Foundation is an important step in Bihar's efforts to become a preferred investment destination. She said that a dedicated food processing park backed by UAE investment could help farmers and industries in Bihar connect with global supply chains and create new opportunities for industrial growth across the state. Focus on Concrete Investment Opportunities Ahead of Rising Bihar 2026 Industries Department Secretary Kundan Kumar said the MoU provides a foundation for structured engagement between Bihar and UAE-based investors in the food processing sector. He said the department looks forward to working closely with AIM Global Foundation to identify concrete investment opportunities and take the partnership forward ahead of Rising Bihar 2026. bihar_raw_news.title: Indian states step up Gulf investor push as UAE becomes gateway to global markets
bihar_raw_news.content: Agencies States race to woo Gulf investors as MP offers extra incentives to big-ticket projects Dubai: Several states in India are intensifying their pursuit of investments from the Gulf, with Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Bihar and Punjab reaching out to sovereign wealth funds , family offices, and companies in the UAE, offering a mix of customised incentives, industrial land, and sector-specific opportunities. These states are increasingly looking at the UAE not just as a source of investment but as a gateway to the entire Gulf and other global markets, pitching their manufacturing, agriculture, mining, logistics and technology capabilities to investors at an annual investment meeting in Dubai and through one-to-one meetings with sovereign investors and business groups. Also read: Indian Inc rushes to align with UAE’s 15% minimum tax as November deadline looms Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav told ET that the state is prepared to offer additional, customised incentives to large investors and wanted UAE companies to use the state as a production base for exports into the Gulf and beyond. "If someone wants to make a significantly large investment, I am willing to give further incentives through the Cabinet Committee for Investment Promotion (CCIP)," said Yadav, adding that the state is prepared to go "out of the way" to support companies bringing in significant investments. The CCIP is the state's top level mechanism for fast tracking large investments and can approve customised support for major industrial projects, including granting specific waivers, exemptions, or deferments on electricity duty, stamp duty, royalty, and government dues. Live Events ET Bureau Vie for gulf capital Notably, Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi has brought forward his UAE visit from December to September amid improving the geopolitical environment and growing activity among other Indian states and investors to attract Gulf capital, Odisha additional chief secretary Hemant Sharma told ET. During his three-day visit, Majhi is slated to meet with sovereign wealth funds, family offices, and prominent investment houses. Majhi's visit comes more than two months after Odisha secured a proposed $11.3 billion integrated aluminium project involving Abu Dhabi-based International Holding Co (IHC) and Adani Group for an aluminium project. "We were supposed to come here a little later this year, but we advanced the visit as the geopolitical situation has largely been resolved, so there is a rush of activity, and we didn't want to miss out on some of the prospective investment," said Sharma. Mineral-rich Odisha is particularly seeking investments in mining and metallurgy, chemicals and petrochemicals, and port-based logistics. "Besides, we are also focusing on new emerging sectors such as semiconductors and electronic data centres for drawing investments," he said. MP CM Yadav, who is in Dubai to meet investors and business groups, has held talks with representatives of companies including DP World, VFS Global, Emaar, Lulu Group, Choithrams, and business chambers besides seeking talks with sovereign wealth funds. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that India has taken fintech journey to new heights, with innovation and inclusion at its core. He said, technologies like Agentic AI, tokenisation and quantum are opening new possibilities in the financial sector. Mr. Modi said this while addressing the seventh edition of the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai this evening. The Prime Minister hailed UPI as a champion of fintech, noting that more than two thousand four hundred crore UPI transactions were recorded in last month. He said Indian UPI is now operational in eleven countries. Mr. Modi stressed that global collaboration in fintech systems should be new goal to reduce transaction costs in remittances. Prime Minister urged stakeholders at the GFF 2026 to use Fintech as a tool for financial inclusion. The Prime Minister also called upon fintech firms to build top notch cyber security, ethical data production standards, strong Fintech regulated industry innovation ecosystem and Fintech Protection Consumer Index. Lauding the country’s remarkable GDP growth in the last quarter, Mr. Modi said, world has gained reassurance from India’s 7.8 percent growth despite challenging global conflicts, uncertainties and stress on global supply chains of energy and commodities. He also highlighted that the Japan Credit Rating Agency has upgraded country’s sovereign credit rating from BBB+ to A- with a stable outlook, returning India to the A rating category after more than three decades. The four-day Global Fintech Fest 2026 is being held in Mumbai from 8th to 11th September. The theme of this year’s fest is Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum – Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 96 Russia backs India’s peace efforts to end Ukraine conflict
national_raw_news.content: Russia today said it would welcome any peace efforts by India to end the Ukraine conflict, noting that Moscow’s strategy aligns closely with New Delhi’s position for a resolution through dialogue and diplomacy. Addressing media at a virtual briefing in New Delhi this afternoon ahead of the BRICS Summit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said they know the position of India on the Ukrainian conflict, and to a great extent, it corresponds with their own position because they do want the solution to the Ukraine conflict by peaceful means, and Russia is open for this process. Mr. Peskov said, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold bilateral talks on the sidelines of BRICS Summit. He said, both leaders are expected to discuss issues of mutual interest. Mr Peskov added that that it will also be an opportunity for President Putin to inform Prime Minister Modi about the situation on the war with Ukraine. He said both leaders are in close personal contact and very pragmatic in their relationship. He said both leaders are able to discuss sensitive matters in open and constructive ways. Replying to a question on trade imbalance netween India and Russia, the Kremlin spokesman said Indian side has raised the issue of trade deficit with Russian side. He further stated that in order to address this imbalance, Russian businesses and companies are now looking for additional goods that can be purchased from India and joint projects that could be launched in India. On import of Russian energy by India, Mr Peskov stated that a new record is set every month but refused to give exact figures. He called sanctions against countries trading with Russia as unacceptable and illegal. He emphasised that it is illegal to attempt to introduce limitations on international trade and to threaten other countries and third parties for doing trade with others. Replying to another query, Mr Peskov maintained that BRICS is against no one. He said BRICS is for participating countries, and for their national interests. He said cooperation in BRICS is based on mutual trust, mutual respect, mutual benefits and trade. He added that these ideals are shared by all the member states. The Kremlin spokesman said that AI would be high on the agenda during the BRICS Summit. He said Russia considers India to be very important partner in the global majority.
